text:
ANA won this one on special teams. All three of its goals came on the power play, going 3 for 4 with the man advantage while FLA went 0 for 4, and that gap in finishing hid how the game was actually played. FLA held the edge in expected goals, 3.76 to 2.59, and in shot attempts, 72 to 42. Simulated replays of every shot gave FLA a 69 percent chance to win, ANA 31.

Cutter Gauthier scored twice on the power play, a snap shot at 16:18 of the first and another at 0:47 of the second, with Leo Carlsson assisting on both. Carter Verhaeghe answered 51 seconds after the first with a tip-in, and Brad Marchand tied it at 2-2 with a wrist shot at 18:10 of the third. Mikael Granlund won it with a tip-in on the power play at 4:14 of overtime, set up by Carlsson and Gauthier. Carlsson finished with three assists and Gauthier with two goals and an assist.

Lukas Dostal made the difference at the other end. ANA's goalie stopped 29 of 31 shots, and the chances against him were worth 3.76 expected goals, so he saved about 1.8 more than an average goalie would have. Jacob Markstrom stopped 17 of 20 for FLA, 0.41 goals worse than expected. At even strength FLA had the clear edge in chance quality, 2.62 to 1.05. ANA blocked 20 shots to FLA's 11, and FLA's 23 giveaways to ANA's 14 gave the home side extra possessions.
